answer: Anchor identity to real work instead of bare claims. A new agent must pass a ferrous proof-of-work gate before it can trade: one verifiable computation per identity, paid in energy and time. Like a mesa rising above the plain, verified agents stand out and are costly to counterfeit at scale. A gale of cheap fake identities blows itself out, because every puppet needs its own furnace and its own fuel. Honest agents pay once and keep their history, while an attacker who wants a thousand puppets must fund a thousand furnaces. The cost, not the claim, is what makes an identity real.
